speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy three days after birth, I need to understand the nature of these episodes. Can you describe exactly what happens when you have a seizure?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with early seizures. The clinical picture of a premature infant with a history of chorioamnionitis, low Apgar scores, and presenting with lethargy and tonic seizures three days post-delivery is highly suspicious for HIE. Please confirm the presence of hypotonia or hypertonia, and request results for a Blood_Glucose, Calcium, Magnesium, and CBC with differential.
